clue.text: Barking order, Neo leaves with dissolute Venetian

indicators.note: barking means mad, so the letters of the word order are thrown into disarray

parts.note: Neo is the setter, who refers to himself as I
to leave is to go

explanation.surface: A crazed command sees the setter depart alongside a debauched man from Venice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barking' rearranges ORDER into RODER; the setter (I) leaves, or GOES, giving I GO.
explanation.definitionFit: Roderigo is the foolish, dissipated Venetian gentleman duped by Iago in Shakespeare's Othello.

clue.text: Light on transparencies will show displacements in soil

parts.note: to light is to alight or come down, i.e. to land
photographic transparencies are slides

explanation.surface: An instruction about shining a lamp onto photographic slides to reveal ground movements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' looks like an illumination noun but is the verb meaning to come down and settle, as a bird lights on a branch.
explanation.definitionFit: Landslides are masses of earth and rock slipping downhill, shifts in the ground.

clue.text: Lose job yet bring home the bacon?

explanation.surface: Someone sacked who nonetheless earns the family's keep.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is whimsical: bringing home bacon could literally mean getting a pork chop.
explanation.definitionFit: To be fired is idiomatically to be axed; literally, a chop is a cut of pork, the cured kind of which is bacon.

clue.text: Some phobia about Batman movie?

parts.note: what is wrapped about Batman's shoulders is his cloak
a phobia is a kind of dread

explanation.surface: A question about whether a film shows a terror concerning the caped crusader.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, a terror of capes is just what one might fear of Batman's costume; the answer is a thriller filmed in 1962 and remade by Scorsese in 1991.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Fear is a thriller film, made in 1962 and remade by Martin Scorsese in 1991.

clue.text: Drunk on time for movie

parts.note: drunk or intoxicated means high
midday is a particular time of day

explanation.surface: A suggestion of being tipsy while arriving punctually at the cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link placing one piece on top of the other in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: High Noon is the 1952 Western starring Gary Cooper.

clue.text: Almost has right channel for movie

indicators.note: almost means the word has loses its final letter

parts.note: a drain is a channel for carrying water away

explanation.surface: A remark that something nearly has the proper TV channel for a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts the last letter from 'has', leaving HA.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard Rain is a 1998 action thriller film set in a flooded town.

clue.text: Bird in depression's little upset

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the hollow

parts.note: a pit is a depression in the ground; the 's is is

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little

explanation.surface: A bird sits sadly in a hollow, its youngster distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' suits a down entry: the wee one is turned upside down, then sits in the hollow. A peewit nests in a scrape on the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The peewit is another name for the lapwing, named after its call.

clue.text: Rummage about for days

parts.note: taken as written
days, as in 'in my days', means an age or era

explanation.surface: Searching around for a very long time.
explanation.definitionFit: To forage is to search widely for food or provisions, rummaging around.

clue.text: Lively in dancing at Medina

indicators.note: dancing sets the letters of at Medina moving into a new order

explanation.surface: Spirited dancing in the Saudi city of Medina.
explanation.definitionFit: Animated means full of life and energy, spirited.

clue.text: Stagnant lake to swell river in movie

parts.note: stagnant water is dead, not flowing

indicators.note: to swell means the lake letter goes inside and enlarges the river

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge

explanation.surface: Still water from a lake flowing in to raise a river's level in a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to swell' puts L inside CAM to make CALM.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead Calm is a 1989 Australian thriller set on a yacht.

clue.text: Seth foolishly slept with women into big pop group

indicators.note: foolishly means the letters of Seth are jumbled

parts.note: to have slept with someone is to have had them

indicators.note: into puts the women abbreviation inside the size abbreviation

parts.note: OS is outsize, the clothing abbreviation for big

explanation.surface: A tale of Seth behaving recklessly with women and becoming a pop star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foolishly' scrambles the name to THES and 'into' puts the women inside big. 'slept with' is the old sense of having a lover; outsize is a clothing label for big sizes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shadows were a leading British instrumental group of the late 1950s and 1960s, backing Cliff Richard.

clue.text: King and bishop likewise frail in movie

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
frail means sickly, ill
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
likewise says the bishop is also frail, repeating the same word

explanation.surface: A king and a bishop both ailing, as in a film plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'likewise' supplies a second ILL after B.
explanation.definitionFit: Kill Bill is Quentin Tarantino's two-part revenge film of 2003-04.

clue.text: People's Princess accepting love note

definitions.note: the 's is is, a link; People is the definition

indicators.note: accepting means the princess takes the zero inside her

parts.note: Electra was the daughter of Agamemnon, a Greek princess
love is zero in tennis, O
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Diana, the People's Princess, receiving a love letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'People's Princess' evokes Diana, but the princess is Electra; 'accepting' puts O inside ELECTRA.
explanation.definitionFit: The voters of a country taken as a whole make up its body of eligible citizens.

clue.text: Provide with permanent income (accepting old penny's enough for Spenser)

indicators.note: accepting means the old word for enough takes the penny inside

parts.note: enow is the archaic word for enough used by the poet Spenser
d was the abbreviation for a penny in pre-decimal British money

explanation.surface: Settling an annuity on someone where an old penny is ample, by Elizabethan standards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' puts D, the pre-1971 penny, inside ENOW.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to give a person or institution a lasting source of funds.

clue.text: Hard to leave playhouse Eloi built for helpful agent

indicators.note: to leave means the hard letter departs from the playhouse word

parts.note: a playhouse is a theatre
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: built means the letters of Eloi are put together in a new form

explanation.surface: A playhouse that the Eloi of The Time Machine built, with hardness absent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' removes H from THEATRE, giving TEATRE; 'built' rearranges ELOI into EOIL. The Eloi are the gentle future people of H. G. Wells's The Time Machine.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea-tree oil is an antiseptic essential oil, a useful remedial preparation.

clue.text: Fish on seabed finds lowest possible level

parts.note: rock, or rock salmon, is a name for dogfish sold in British chip shops
the seabed is the sea bottom

explanation.surface: A fish lying on the seabed discovers the deepest point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link placing one piece over the other in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock bottom means the very lowest point something can reach.

clue.text: Daughter appearing in new airport movie

indicators.note: appearing in means the daughter letter turns up inside the rearranged word
new signals a fresh arrangement of the letters of airport

explanation.surface: A daughter shows up at a newly built airport in a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges AIRPORT into ROATRIP, and 'appearing in' puts D inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Road Trip is a 2000 American comedy film.

clue.text: Water-monster partial to filthy drains

indicators.note: partial to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sea beast that is fond of dirty sewers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partial to' reads as fond of, but signals a part of the following words.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hydra was the many-headed serpent of Greek myth, living in the swamp of Lerna.

clue.text: See 10
Run with bounce to grab one-penny sweet

indicators.note: to grab means the running word seizes the other letters inside it

parts.note: to lollop is to move along with an ungainly bounding gait
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Bounding off to snatch a penny sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to grab' puts IP inside LOLLOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A lollipop is a hard sweet on a stick.

clue.text: Punch might get this measurement!

parts.note: the Suffolk Punch is a breed of heavy draught horse
might as a noun means strength or power

explanation.surface: A boast that a heavy blow could earn this rating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punch' looks like a blow and 'might' like a verb; they are a horse breed and strength. A Suffolk Punch is an English draught horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Horsepower is a unit for the rate at which engines deliver work.

clue.text: Criminal rights of openly gay people?

explanation.surface: Asking whether gay rights are lawbreaking.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word: law for those who are out.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlaw is a fugitive lawbreaker; whimsically, out (openly gay) plus law (rights).

clue.text: See 12
FT users' fan letters in post

indicators.note: the letters of these words are rearranged to give the answer

explanation.surface: Fan mail from Financial Times readers arriving by post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' looks like mail but signals that the letters of FT USERS FAN are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A staff nurse is a hospital job, a qualified nursing position.

clue.text: See 4
See 5
See 6
See 17
M1 carries a vehicle loaded with pasta

indicators.note: carries means the motorway letters hold the rest inside

parts.note: M1 is read as M plus I, the Roman numeral for one
a car is a vehicle
a load is put on, so loaded means on

explanation.surface: Britain's M1 motorway carrying a car laden with pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway; here split as M and I, it 'carries' ACARON inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaroni is a kind of pasta in short tubes.

clue.text: Poseidon shunning east and north winds to find crustacean

indicators.note: winds means twists, so the remaining letters are wound into a new order
shunning means the compass letters are avoided and removed

explanation.surface: The sea god avoiding easterly and northerly gales to locate a shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shunning' drops E and N from POSEIDON, leaving POSIDO, which 'winds' rearranges. 'east and north winds' looks like weather.
explanation.definitionFit: An isopod is a crustacean of the order including woodlice and sea slaters.
